overview: This file comprises a State Department forwarding letter and its enclosed instruction of November 29, 1949, concerning the seizure of Japanese fishing vessels by Chinese patrols. The Department asks its representatives in Hong Kong and Taiwan to press Chinese authorities to recognize the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) as the sole authority over Japanese high-seas fishing during the occupation, halt further seizures, and release detained vessels and crews. The instruction reviews diplomatic protests since 1948, Chinese claims based on traditional fishing interests and an executive order, the fatal sinking of the Akashi Maru No. 105, and the legal and economic arguments to be used in approaching the Chinese Government.

subfiles.title: Forwarding letter to MacDonald on Chinese seizures of Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: John J. MacDonald, American Consul General, Taipei
subfiles.about: Forwards the Department’s instruction to Hong Kong and directs a supplementary approach to the Taiwan authorities concerning seized Japanese fishing vessels and crews.
subfiles.summary: State asks MacDonald to press Taiwan authorities to end seizures and release detained Japanese fishing vessels and crews, mirroring an instruction to Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Strong on Chinese seizures and SCAP authority over Japanese fishing
subfiles.from: W. Walton Butterworth, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Robert C. Strong, American Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, Hong Kong
subfiles.about: Directs an approach to Chinese officials asserting SCAP’s exclusive enforcement authority over Japanese high-seas fishing and requesting an end to Chinese seizures and the release of vessels and crews.
subfiles.summary: Instruction reports Chinese patrols seized eleven Japanese fishing vessels since May 1949 (only two returned), including the sunk Akashi Maru No. 105 (eight deaths); it rejects China's legal claims and instructs Strong to press for SCAP's sole authority and vessel release.

interest: Shows postwar China-U.S. clashes over SCAP's exclusive authority amid Chinese seizures of Japanese fishing vessels.
